title: It Is the Lord
speaker: Jonathan Baird
summary: Jesus is present even when we don't recognize him. He is patient, he reveals himself, and when he does, throw yourself into the sea.
exhortation: A few things came to mind as I read this. First, Jesus is present, but we don't always recognize it. I get into situations and lean on my own understanding and experience. It actually gets worse the older I get, because now I think I know things. So I go to my own strength and my own thinking: how can I solve this? Instead of going straight to the Savior who is always present and has never left. He told us he would send his Spirit and that it would be better, because then he would be with us always. But sometimes we just sit there trying to muscle it through on our own.

Second, look at how patient Jesus is. This is almost a humorous passage. I can imagine Jesus chuckling to himself: "Guys, I'm right here." They're going about their work, sad, maybe ready to put an arm around this stranger and say, "You should have known Jesus. He was a great guy." And Jesus is patient and slow to anger. He brings them along and gives them instruction.
Then finally Jesus reveals himself. I am very grateful that in my ignorance, foolishness and self-centeredness, Jesus reveals himself. He doesn't leave us where we are. We serve a God who intervenes.

And then comes the response. When Peter, by God's grace, sees that it is the Lord, he throws himself into the sea. He throws himself at Jesus wholeheartedly, with total abandon. He isn't thinking about his great catch or how cold the water is. He's thinking, "I have seen the Lord." Let that be true of us. When Jesus reveals himself, let's throw ourselves into the sea and run to him. Let's resist the temptation to lean on our own strength and understanding, and trust in the Lord alone.
prayer: Jesus, thank you for opening our eyes. We were blind to your glory, goodness, love and grace until you called out to us, pursued us and healed our blindness so that we could see you for who you are.

As we go through our day, help us lift our eyes to you: to see you in your word, in creation, in other people, and at work in our lives and the lives of others. Open our eyes to who you are and what you are doing, so that we are about the work of your kingdom. What can we say but thank you, Lord? In Jesus' name, amen.
